scope: Five-variant source-reviewed Bayesian posterior group with dedicated posterior-kernel and Bayes density theorem evidence.

rows.query: Resolved all five registered PDFs; inspected p0335 p7, p0519 p10, p1433 p4, p1691 p5 and p1825 p9 with their preserved variants and source-issue notes. Searched Bayes/posterior in pinned Probability/Kernel and ConditionalProbability; inspected Posterior:60–82,203–238,266–305 and CondDistrib:51–88. Checked withDensity and lintegral bodies. Opened the two new official posterior declaration URLs and matched all displayed source lines to the pinned archive.
rows.result: posterior is a conditional-law kernel on a nonempty standard Borel parameter space for a finite prior and finite sampling kernel. posterior_eq_withDensity gives the prior-weighting Bayes identity almost everywhere under the prior predictive law, with CountableOrCountablyGenerated and component-to-predictive absolute continuity. Its density is relative to the predictive law, so identifying it with a paper likelihood divided by marginal likelihood needs an additional Radon–Nikodym calculation. withDensity/lintegral can express the explicit normalized formulas on positive finite evidence. No equality for every observed sample or fixed true law follows solely from predictive-almost-everywhere equality.
rows.gap: Instantiate each sampling kernel and parameter space, identify the normalized likelihood density and justify the posterior version under its stated observation law.

comparisons.D5: For p0335 (2.5), retain the hierarchical prior, disjoint model tags, parameter map T and likelihood p_n(T(theta),Y). Build the normalized withDensity measure on positive finite evidence. posterior supplies a conditional-law kernel after proving standard Borel/nonempty parameter space and finite measurable sampling kernel; its almost-everywhere density theorem is not an unconditional samplewise identity or a convention at zero/infinite evidence. It does not select a variational minimizer.
comparisons.D8: For p0519 (16), form the dependent Markov-path likelihood product p_D,f(X_(i-1)D,X_iD), retaining the explicit joint Borel measurability and B in S. The initial law is common to all parameters; its cancellation does not make path observations iid. Identify the sampling kernel’s predictive-relative density with this likelihood divided by its prior integral before applying posterior_eq_withDensity. Keep f coordinates distinct from theta coordinates used for other posterior expectations, and justify the version when evaluating under a fixed true diffusivity law.
comparisons.D11: For p1433 D11, posterior directly provides the structural conditional law of f given X once the function parameter space is nonempty standard Borel and the model is a measurable finite kernel. Dominated Bayes formula requires the corresponding measurable density representation and normalizer identification. The paper analyzes the result under fixed P_f0^(n), not the prior predictive law; an almost-everywhere posterior identity under the latter does not alone justify every true-law statement or supply function-space posterior contraction.
comparisons.D12: For p1691 D12, the prior is on probability measures on R^d and may depend on n. Use the n-fold product convolution-density likelihood f_Y(Y_i), not a likelihood for directly observed signals, and prove measurability of the law-valued parameterization and positive finite evidence. The regular-kernel construction needs the corresponding standard Borel realization; posterior_eq_withDensity gives a predictive-almost-everywhere identity after density identification. Later posteriors of observation laws require a measurable convolution pushforward rather than a new prior or silently identifying signal and observation laws.
comparisons.D14: For p1825 (21), weight the Gaussian prior on initial states V by exp(-one-half the sum of squared Euclidean R^2 residuals) and supply its marginal normalizer. Keep the source u_theta(X_i,t_i) argument ordering as printed, including the recorded discrepancy with model (19). The resulting kernel is a posterior for the nonlinear PDE observation experiment after measurability/space proofs; the generic constructor does not assert it is Gaussian or prove MCMC behavior. Its defining conditional-law equivalence is almost everywhere under the model marginal and needs the appropriate version for fixed P_theta0^N analysis.
